note: 39 of the corpus's 52 columns. The 13 dropped ones are listed above WITH THE REASON each was dropped, because three of them are the point of this model: `Unnamed: 0`, `Seq` and `Offset` are integer row counters, and refitting this identical configuration with them restored reproduces the 99.6-99.7% accuracies published for this corpus while dropping them costs about 24 points. Those figures are recorded as `leak_counterfactual_*` in models/metrics.json and are re-measured on every run. A SEPARATE AND LEGITIMATE MATTER, stated because the numbers look alarming next to that: 21 of the 39 kept features still clear the 0.90 one-vs-rest AUC threshold after all 13 drops, led by `Rate` at 0.9941 on ICMPFlood and `AckDat` at 0.9928 on HTTPFlood. Those are real flow statistics rather than bookkeeping columns: each attack class in this corpus was produced by a different tool against a different service, so packet rate, ACK timing, TTL and TCP window separating them is the signal an intrusion detector is meant to use. They are reported and kept. The three identifiers cleared the same threshold while describing only where a row sits in a file, and that is the distinction this file exists to make - see `single_feature_leak_check` in models/metrics.json for the full measured list. `categorical_vocabularies` is the ordinal encoding the five string columns were fitted under; index into the list, and use `missing_value` for anything absent or unseen. It is published rather than re-derived because a vocabulary rebuilt from different rows would remap codes the ONNX thresholds were fitted against.
